findings: Server-side Zenoh read boundary (mini_api, mini_runtime, mini_zenoh) enforces signed Telegram initData validation before and after observation within the 5s deadline, restricts the optional topic parameter (<=512 bytes) exclusively to MiniZenohBrowser, bounds configuration to 1..256 grants and <=20 unique exact topics per user, and returns 403 topic_access_denied without querying Zenoh for ungranted, cross-user, or wildcard keys.

Payload handling in mini_zenoh validates UTF-8 scalar values (rejecting C0, DEL, and C1 control characters except HT/LF/CR), enforces the <=32768-byte payload ceiling and <=100 observation field cap, and losslessly splits multi-byte codepoints into <=2048-byte parts with zero-padded labels for deterministic lexicographic ordering.

zenoh/rest.gleam and zenoh_rest_ffi.erl enforce the fixed nas-1.tail55d152.ts.net:8080 endpoint, 3000ms deadline, segment/character allowlist (no wildcards, empty segments, or dot-segments), c3i/a2a PUT prohibition, and strict single-sample envelope decoding with exact key match and explicit zenoh_no_reply vs error separation.

Client script in mini_app_routes.gleam renders exclusively via DOM textContent and Option constructors, enforces a <=20 unique topic bound, and implements completion-based 2-second single-flight polling bounded to 5 minutes that halts on manual stop, topic change, auth absence/expiry, HTTP/network/unavailable errors, visibilitychange (document.hidden), and pagehide.

Non-blocking client note: clicking manual #mini-refresh while a 2-second live-refresh timer is pending does not clearTimeout(timer) at the start of refresh(), which can schedule an extra poll tick; however, busy/queued gating preserves single-flight fetch execution and liveUntil preserves the 5-minute ceiling.
